body:
## Problem

`integrate.fold` folds **every** accepted bundle onto the target's integration branch — "the cumulative accepted patches (waves 0..k) in order" (`integrate.py:132-162`) — and the next wave's Do worktree and PRs then base off that branch. Wave membership, not dependency, decides what a PR sits on top of.

The result is that a bundle with no declared relationship to anything in an earlier wave still gets a PR whose base carries all of that earlier work. Consequences:

- **The PR misrepresents its own change.** A reviewer opening it sees a base branch containing unrelated bundles. The diff is right, but "what this is built on" is not.
- **Unnecessary coupling to the re-fold.** `fold` rebuilds the branch from the target base on every call, so every open PR based on it goes stale at the next wave boundary — old `pdca-integrate:*` commits fall out of the base's ancestry (host DCO red) and an overlapping later bundle turns a PR CONFLICTING against its own folded content (getwyrd/wyrd#675/#676, 2026-08-01, the reason getwyrd/wyrd-pdca switched to merge mode). Every independent bundle dragged onto that branch is exposed to a failure mode it has no reason to be exposed to.
- **It discards information the harness already has.** Briefs already declare relationships: `Depends on`, `Depends on (merged)`, and `Stacks on` (#123, which is explicitly "build this bundle on top of a prerequisite's branch and publish it as a separate stacked PR"). The wave planner uses these to *order* bundles, but the fold ignores them when choosing a base.

## Proposal (sketch)

Make the integration base dependency-scoped rather than wave-scoped.

- A bundle that declares no dependency on any bundle accepted earlier in the run bases its PR on the **real target base**, exactly as a single-bundle run would. No integration branch involvement.
- A bundle that does declare one bases on a branch carrying its **transitive prerequisites only** — not the whole cumulative set. Whether that is one branch per dependency chain or one per bundle is the design question; the existing `Stacks on` mechanics are the obvious starting point, generalised from a single chain to a prerequisite closure.
- Wave ordering stays as it is: waves still decide *when* a bundle builds; this changes only *what its PR is based on*.

Independent bundles are the common case in most batches, so this should leave most PRs on the real base, shrink the re-fold blast radius to the chains that genuinely need stacking, and make each stacked PR's base mean something a reviewer can read.

Related: #395 (undeclared same-wave overlap) — a dependency-scoped base makes an undeclared overlap fail earlier and more locally, since an unrelated patch is no longer silently present in a bundle's base.

## Done when
- (from #630) Real git, stack mode: wave 0 = {A, Z}, Z unrelated; B `Depends on: A` only. After the run, B's PR branch must not contain any commit of Z's branch, so closing Z's PR keeps Z's work off `main` whatever happens to B.

comments.body:
Moving the reproducing test from #630 here. #630 will be closed as a duplicate of this issue: its only real fix is this one, where the integration line carries only a PR's declared prerequisites.

**What #630 showed.** Since #593 (PR #619), a wave>0 PR opens against the real base (`template/src/pdca_harness/publish.py:282` on `main` @ `b5f5c29`) and is cut from the run's integration line, which holds every earlier-wave bundle of the target (`integrate.py:21-24`). Merging any wave>0 PR therefore lands every earlier-wave bundle on the base, including one whose own PR the human closed. Closing a bundle's PR does not keep its work off the target.

**Test for this issue** (real git, stack mode, the `StackFoldGit` fixture in `template/tests/test_integrate_stack_bases.py`):

- wave 0 = {A, Z}, where Z is unrelated; B has `Depends on: A` only.
- Publish A and Z, fold [A, Z], publish B cut from the line (`cut_from=f"origin/{LINE}"`).
- Assert that B's PR branch contains no commit of Z's branch: `self._ancestor(self._tip("fix/Z"), self._tip("fix/B"))` must be false. It is true on `main` today.

So closing Z's PR keeps Z's work off `main` whatever happens to B.

title: stack mode bases every PR in a wave on every other — only declared dependencies need a stacked base
